newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 21.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5649. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- The South Koren government on Thursday announced $6 million in food aid to North Korea.
- South Korean leaders, including President Kim Young-sam, extended condolences to China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, who died Wednesday in Beijing.
- The South Korean government announced Thursday that it will approve $6 million in food aid to North Korea through the United Nations World Food Program (WFP).
- President Kim Young-sam on Thursday issued a special statement expressing his and the Korean people's deep condolences over the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping.

- South Korea is hopeful that China will soon allow a high-ranking North Korean defector to fly to Seoul but his departure could be delayed pending the funeral of late Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, government officials said on Thursday.
- The government is expected to allow a North Korean defector to fly to Seoul from China after Deng Xiaoping's funeral.
- President Kim Young-sam's son, Hyun-chul, to be summoned by prosecutors over Hanbo scandal.

- President Kim Young-sam is expected to apologise about the Hanbo loan scandal and try to dispell rumours regarding the role his son, Hyun-chul, played in the scandal during an address to the nation on Tuesday, sources said.
